newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea says stricken firms must be liquidated.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says stricken firms must be liquidated.

text.p: South Korea's Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik, in a statement issued three days after the collapse of Sammi Steel Co, said on Friday companies that cannot stand by themselves must be liquidated.
"We must bravely liquidate companies that are operating on the margins," he said, in a reference to companies being artificially propped up.
"Companies must strengthen specialisation and improve managerial transparency," the statement said.

On Tuesday Sammi Steel filed for court protection along with its marketing affiliate Sammi Corp. Three other unlisted units of South Korea's 26th largest conglomerate, Sammi Group, sought protection on Friday.
Sammi's collapse followed the failure in January of South Korea's second largest steelmaker, Hanbo Steel Co.
The stock market has been buffeted by fears of a domino-effect of corporate failures.
Huge exposure by banks to Sammi and Hanbo have sparked jitters among foreign lenders about the health of the country's banking sector, raising the cost of overseas funds.
Kang, who took office in a cabinet reshuffle this month prompted by a loans scandal linked to the Hanbo failure, said the government would seek to undo the damage.
"The government will seek measures needed to stabilise financial markets and strengthen international credibility," he said. He gave no details.
On Thursday Kang vowed to slash government spending and tax revenue this year to keep inflation under control as the economy slows.
"Even if economic growth slows below five percent, we will change the economic structure from the bottom," his statement said on Friday.
A central bank official on Friday revised downwards predicted gross domestic product (GDP) growth this year to 6.0 percent from 6.4 percent.
